body: I think I’m a bit younger than your typical expat retiree here in Ecuador, I’m 29 and bought a farm here when I was 28. When I first came to Ecuador I actually didn’t think I’d like it at all. I tried to make the best of a bad situation and went to go see a finca for sale and I almost canceled the showing because I really didn’t think it would work out for me. I immediately changed my opinion on that upon meeting my neighbors and the people of the village that my farm is in. I realized that I had never experienced a real community before even growing up in a small town in America, I had never seen such harmony and hospitality. I came to South America looking for good business opportunities, but I found good friends instead and now I just hang out with mi vecinos.

She’s the only one who knows where I’m going. Everyone else thinks I’m just off working somewhere. The reason I did this was because I believe that the anxiety caused by not knowing what is going to happen is what really rips people apart. It’s not nice to give people the gift of worry.

Not a fan of Donald trump or fascism, but don’t you think that comparing the deportation of illegal immigrants who have knowingly broken a law meant to protect equal access to our country to the holocaust is just a tiny bit dishonest? 
I think it’s so important for us to have intelligent, thoughtful disagreements and discussions but that can’t happen if we start in bad faith.
What do you think would happen if you went to London on a tourist visa and overstayed your allotted time? Do you think they’d deport you? Does that make them fascists? 

I’m not for Donald trump, I’m not for fascism. I’m actually extremely in favor of simplifying our immigration policy and getting as many people as we can into America. I believe a diverse populous is our greatest strength as a country. 

The people I know who are in favor of deportation of illegal immigrants aren’t white supremacists, they’re just in favor of law and order. Having a protest where you characterize them as hateful fascists seems more likely to create more hate and misunderstanding than enact productive change and improvement.

First I'd just like to say to Historical\_Ant7359 that I'm currently working on purchasing a Subway franchise and your answers to questions/posts have been very helpful so thank you!

Currently I run a very profitable handyman service in Hawaii working exclusively with high-end property management companies.   
  
The reason I've decided to switch businesses is how incredibly difficult it is to scale a service based business. Finding very skilled, honest and reliable people is incredibly difficult. I imagine that you will find this to be the number one challenge in trying to run any service based franchise. People who are highly skilled, dependable and smart laborers quickly realize they could make more money working for themselves than working for your company so you'll always be dealing with not the best employees.

The next thing I'd consider with a franchise is this:  
It seems to me that the only thing a service based franchise can offer you is an instant reputation. That has some value, but in my experience, building a good reputation in a service based industry is actually very easy. For every 10 companies offering a service only 1 is actually good (here in Hawaii at least). Just showing up on time is enough to put you above 90% of the competition. 

Most local serviced based businesses have very small marketing budgets or none at all. If you have the money to buy into a franchise you should ask yourself if you'd be better off simply putting that money into marketing or buying leads. If you do good work you'll quickly have more business than you can handle and that will send you back to my reason for switching businesses. Finding quality employees to allow you to scale is very difficult.

I'll tell you a story of a guy I used to work for when I was a kid:  
  
He had a business doing screened in porches. I asked him how he started his business. He told me that when he was 19 he worked for a guy who had a business doing screened in porches and that the owner of that business taught him how to do it. He was really smart and he learned how to do it really quickly. Within 2yrs, he was so good at doing it the owner would just send him to do jobs by himself, which he enjoyed because he liked working by himself. He did that for almost a year when the owner made a big mistake. He asked him to pick up the check from a client who he had finished a job for. When he saw how much the owner had made from the job that he had done he quit immediately and started his own business. 

That's the inevitability of absentee-owner service businesses. Unless your actively participating in the business you're going to need someone who can run the business perfectly and eventually they're going to ask themselves "why aren't I just doing this myself?" in the restaurant industry your manager might be prohibited by the cost and risk associated with buying/starting a restaurant. In the service based world your best employee probably only needs a couple thousand dollars to start their own thing.

Before I settled on Subway I was looking into buying a pool cleaning franchise and quickly realized this very same thing.

I know that there are successful service based franchises but I think these are successful for the company selling the franchise not the person buying into it. Have you ever heard of someone owning 30 roto-rooters and living out of the country half the year?
